fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Loyalty Survey
fields.features_subheading: One prompt builds the survey and the member table behind it. A later prompt changes the questions before the next round goes out.
fields.feature_1:
Questions for each part of the program

Name the parts members touch, such as earning points, redeeming, and the reward catalog. Emergent drafts a rating and a comment for each, and a prompt rewords any question.
fields.feature_2:
Tier and points balance on every answer

The app reads each member's tier and points balance from your loyalty platform through its API. Each response carries both, so Gold members sort apart from new ones.
fields.feature_3:
Answers in a database you own

Each response is a row in a database you own, dated and tagged with the store. Put this spring's reward ratings beside last spring's, or compare two stores in one month.
fields.feature_4:
Low redemption scores reach the store

Pick the score that needs a reply. When a member rates a redemption 1 or 2, the app sends that store's manager a Slack message with the reward and the member's comment.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen on a phone

Members answer one question per screen from a link in their receipt email, on a phone. Emergent puts no cap on responses, so every member in the whole program can answer.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and your codebase

Host the survey on your own domain, included in Emergent and paid for in credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep each version there.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Rewards Programs Use Surveys
fields.tab_content_1:
For 702 members, a 10-stamp card took too long

Each spring, Saffery Coffee asks its 4,200 rewards members about earning stamps, redeeming them, and the drinks on offer. This year 1,316 answered, and 702 said the 10-stamp card took too long to fill. Marketing lead Nuala Gartside cut the card to 8 stamps before summer.
fields.tab_content_2:
Points expired before 97 members reached any reward

Ivelbrook Outfitters sent 3 questions to the 640 members with no purchase in 120 days. Of the 214 who answered, 97 said their points expired before they reached a reward. Points had lasted 12 months. Loyalty manager Bettany Sumner extended them to 24 months for every member.
fields.tab_content_3:
In a vote on the next reward, a free nail trim won

Wrayford Pet Supply asked its members to choose 1 of 4 new rewards, with one vote each, and 1,038 voted. A free nail trim took 412 votes, ahead of a birthday treat with 301. Store operations lead Fintan Arbery added the nail trim to the reward catalog at 500 points.
fields.tab_content_4:
With no loaves left by noon, Elm Street scored low 29 times

Hollinmoor Bakery asks 2 questions after every reward a member redeems. In March, 38 of 512 redemptions scored 1 or 2, and 29 came from the Elm Street store, where the free loaf ran out by noon. Each low score sent store manager Lysander Kindred a Slack message. He now holds back 12 loaves a day for rewards.

fields.howto_title: How to Write Loyalty Survey Questions
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write loyalty program survey questions that members finish and that point to one change in the program.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick one part of the program to test
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pull member status from the platform
fields.howto_step_1_des: Give each survey one focus: earning, redeeming, the reward catalog, or tiers. A survey that covers all four in depth runs long, and members quit halfway. Put that focus in your prompt, and Emergent drafts the questions around it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Skip questions the program can already answer, like a member's tier, join date, and points balance. Attach those from your loyalty platform instead. A Gold member's complaint about expiry then reads differently from a new member's, and nobody types their status.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask how hard a reward is to reach before asking whether the rewards are worth it. A member who has never redeemed cannot rate the catalog. Put both questions on the same 1 to 5 scale, and the answers compare directly.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Members who stopped buying give you less time than active ones. Offer a short list of reasons, such as points expiring or moving away, and then an open box. The list makes answers countable, and the box catches the reason you missed.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Test a new reward with a vote
fields.howto_step_5_des: Before adding a reward, list a few options and let members pick one. Check each vote against your member list to keep it to one per member. The winner shows what members want to spend points on, before you set its price in points.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Name who reads the low scores
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide which score calls for action, such as a redemption rated 1 or 2, and name one person per store to read it. A manager who sees the comment that day can fix a stock problem before the weekend rush.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Send the survey to one store's members for two weeks before the whole program gets it. Read every answer, reword any question members skip, and check that tier and points arrive on each response. Then open it to every member.

plan.angle: The pages ranking for loyalty program survey questions are generic customer satisfaction lists with one or two loyalty lines. This page treats the loyalty program itself as the subject: questions on earning, redeeming and reward value, each answer tied to the member's tier and points balance, plus the three other surveys a program manager runs: a lapsed-member check, a vote on the next reward, and a two-question check after each redemption.
